decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys (HEAs) has been focused on understanding their microstructure, phase formation, and resulting mechanical and thermal properties. Recent studies have explored the effects of processing routes, such as mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, and additive manufacturing, on the microstructure and properties of HEAs. Additionally, the oxidation behavior and radiation resistance of HEAs have been investigated. The trend suggests a growing interest in designing HEAs with improved thermal stability, radiation resistance, and oxidation resistance for extreme temperature applications.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in understanding HEAs, there is still a need to overcome the limited accuracy of available analytical predictions and their restriction to perfect, defect-free crystals. The development of a predictive approach that can accurately model the behavior of HEAs in the 0-200 K and 300-1200 K regimes, considering the effects of defects and impurities, remains an unsolved challenge.
decision.lever: development of a machine learning model that incorporates atomic-scale simulations and experimental data to predict the thermal and electrical conductivity of HEAs
decision.why: The development of a machine learning model that incorporates atomic-scale simulations and experimental data can help to improve the accuracy of predictive approaches for HEAs. By leveraging the strengths of both simulation and experimentation, such a model can provide a more comprehensive understanding of the behavior of HEAs in various temperature regimes and can help to overcome the limitations of existing analytical approaches.
